The Fundamental Memory Ceiling of Noisy Quantum Reservoirs
Markus Baumann1,∗
1Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Geschwister-Scholl-Platz 1, 80539 München, Germany
(Dated: October 18, 2026)
Fresh qubits, not size, set how long a noisy quantum reservoir can remember its inputs. Withk
input qubits reinitialized per time step, the longest memory any reservoir can attain under depo-
larizing noise isexp[Θ(k)] time steps, whatever its size, dynamics, and input encoding. A universal
upper bound and an explicit reservoir that attains the exponential scaling establish this optimal
resource law. The bound rests only on the entropy budget of each time step, so it applies to any
noisy quantum dynamics supplied with fresh qubits, from quantum reservoirs to measurement-free
error correction.
Introduction.—Reservoir computing processes time
series with the transient dynamics of a fixed physical
system, the reservoir: inputs are injected into it, and
only a linear readout is trained [1–5]. Quantum reser-
voir computing (QRC) uses interacting qubits for this
purpose [6–8] and has been realized on superconducting
processors with up to 120 qubits [9–13]. For temporal
tasks, memory is the decisive resource. A reservoir that
forecasts a time series can use an input only as long as
